title: PLA ADIZ Activity Eases to 9 Sorties as Han Kuang 42 Concludes
detail: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 9 PLA aircraft sorties, 12 PLAN vessels and 2 official ships operating around Taiwan in the 24-hour window ending 06:00 (UTC+8) on August 14, 2026. Six of the nine sorties crossed the Taiwan Strait median line, entering the central, southwestern and eastern sectors of Taiwan's ADIZ. Activity eased from the previous day's 18-sortie spike, while the PLAN vessel count (12) reached the highest level of the window. The report landed on the final day of Taiwan's Han Kuang 42 live-fire exercise.

title: Taiwan Concludes 10-Day Han Kuang 42 Exercise, Its Largest War Games Since 1984
detail: Taiwan concluded its 10-day Han Kuang 42 live-fire exercise on August 14, 2026, at a closing ceremony at Bo'ai Camp in Taipei attended by Chief of the General Staff Mei Chia-shu, service chiefs and regional commanders. Defense Minister Wellington Koo praised the troops and urged officers to address issues identified during the drills to further strengthen combat readiness. Running since August 5, the exercise — described as Taiwan's largest-scale war games since 1984 — for the first time employed a fully 'unscripted,' free-play format with fully operational command centers at every level, forcing units to respond to dynamic orders based on developing simulated threats rather than a pre-set script, while maintaining strict safety discipline during high-intensity maneuvers. The cycle included the first operational participation of M1A2T Abrams tanks, activation of roughly 5,000 reservists, President Lai's August 9 troop inspection in Taoyuan, and the closing mobile-internet-slowdown and Navy-Coast Guard anti-blockade drills.

title: Taiwan Navy and Coast Guard Hold First-Ever Joint Anti-Blockade Drill
detail: As the closing exercise of the Han Kuang 42 cycle, Taiwan's Navy and Coast Guard completed their first-ever joint anti-blockade drill on August 14, 2026, escorting a simulated merchant vessel carrying essential supplies to eastern Taiwan under a 2nd Combat Theater Command scenario in which enemy forces infiltrate a port to disrupt the delivery. A Yushan-class landing platform dock played the role of the merchant ship approaching from waters off Taiwan's east coast; the Navy dispatched a surface action group and light surface forces to escort it, while Coast Guard patrol vessels and CM21 armored vehicles helped secure the transfer of supplies, which were offloaded at Hualien Port and Suao Port using civilian cranes and flatbed trucks alongside military logistics assets. The drill was designed to test inter-agency coordination for keeping wartime supplies flowing to Taiwan's east coast under a blockade scenario reminiscent of China's August 2022 encirclement exercises.

title: Legislature Passes 2026 Budget After Record 266-Day Delay, Drone Funding Intact
detail: Taiwan's Legislative Yuan passed the central government's 2026 budget on August 14, 2026, approving NT$2.9869 trillion (about US$93 billion) in spending — the longest delay to clear a central government budget in Taiwan's democratic history. The Cabinet had submitted the bill on August 31, 2025, with a statutory deadline of end-November 2025, but review dragged on for 266 days amid deadlock between the Lai administration and the opposition-controlled legislature. The final package came in about 1.7% below what the Lai administration had sought, but the NT$63.4 billion drone-industry development and procurement budget passed intact, despite earlier Kuomintang threats to cut it by as much as 70%. The delay had left large parts of the government, including defense procurement timelines, operating on stopgap funding for much of 2026.
